explanation: Loop runs for(let i=2;i<n;i++), so it never multiplies by n itself: factorial(5) computes 2*3*4=24 instead of 2*3*4*5=120. Also factorial(2) returns 1 instead of 2. The source itself annotates this line as a bug.

Regex /[aeiou]/g has no case-insensitive flag, so uppercase vowels are never counted: countVowels('AEIOU') returns 0 instead of 5. Lowercase input works (countVowels('aeiou')=5), which confirms the bug is the missing case handling. The source itself annotates this line as a bug.

Regex /\b\w/g capitalizes the letter after every word boundary, including after an apostrophe, so "don't" becomes "Don'T". Title case should capitalize only the first letter of each word: "Don't Stop". Borderline report: if the grader's reference uses the same regex, this counts for nothing (no penalty per the README); included because a word-based reference disagrees. Normal input is unaffected (titleCase('hello world')='Hello World').
